units.title: Power off in Gilliver last night, three times and then for an hour.
units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Power went at ten to two, came back, went again about half two, back, then at quarter past three it went and stayed off till twenty past four. I was up for the boat anyway. Whole front was dark. Freezer's fine, I didn't open it. Anyone know if it's the same as the storm or something new?

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Overnight readings for what they're worth: mist formed at 23:40, visibility down to 400 m by 01:30, relative humidity 98 to 99 per cent from midnight to dawn, wind calm. Dew on every surface. Salt crust from the storm on the windward posts was dripping by three. If the co-op says salt and dew, I'd have to say the weather backs them up for last night.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: I have made this the thread for the Gilliver outages. The co-op's notice says three short interruptions and a longer one, about 380 properties, cause under investigation. Please post what you experienced and where. For anything dangerous, ring the co-op's emergency line, not this forum. Thank you. Pell (admin).

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: That's about as clean a case for salt-fog flashover as you'll get. What would we expect to see? Trips on a calm, saturated night after a westerly gale, concentrated on the section nearest the spray, in the small hours when dew peaks. That's what happened. Washing should fix it. If it doesn't, then we'd have something to talk about.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Lisle was unaffected, we're on the island's own cable from the other side. But my friend on Front Row rang this morning to say it was the last straw, after the water. She sat up with her oil lamp, which her mother left her. I offered to come across again. She says she'd rather I brought a flask.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Convenient that the 'cause' is the weather, which nobody can check except one man with a station in his garden. The Gilliver feeder is the line that faces the Holm. It came through a whole storm without a trip and then fails on the first calm night. I'm only asking. Ask yourselves why a power company would want to keep a village dark.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Gil, it failed on the first calm night because salt only flashes over when it's wet and the wind isn't washing it. In a storm, the rain cleans the insulators as fast as the spray dirties them. The calm night afterwards is exactly when you'd expect trouble. And a power company is paid to keep the lights on. It doesn't want a village dark, it wants fewer complaints.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Tollinby fine, for once. For anyone in Gilliver with kids and a freezer: 1. tape the freezer shut with a note on it, 2. torches on the stairs, not candles, 3. a battery radio is the best thing in a cut, Sound FM tells you what's happening before the co-op does, 4. a head torch is worth three ordinary ones.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: I didn't notice it at all, I'm afraid. I was asleep, and my front window lamp is paraffin, so it stayed lit, and in the morning the clocks were all wrong. My neighbour says the whole front was dark except for a few windows. I said yes, the lamps. It was quite a nice thing to know, in a way.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Not Gilliver but related: Brackwater jct temp lights were dead this morning, no red, no green, nothing, and everyone just sort of took turns. Smoothest that junction's run in a month. Co-op lad said they're on the Brackwater east line. Recommend permanent power cut, purely for traffic flow.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Patrol notes from last night, since people are asking. Walked the Gilliver feeder by torch from the sea wall to the Brackwater tee, about 3.2 km, 02:00 to 04:40. Salt on the windward insulator strings near the wall, yes, like the weather station said. No birds, no branches, no tracking or burn marks on the strings we could see. The breaker reclosed twice and held, then locked out. Washing starts tomorrow.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: What Tess said. I'll go this far: there was salt, and salt does trip lines. I've seen flashover after storms for twenty-five years and it leaves you something to look at, a scorch, a tracked string, a smell. Last night we had nothing to look at. That's all I'm saying, and that's more than I'm meant to say.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Fair point, Garvey, and I respect it. Light flashover on wet salt doesn't always mark a string, though, especially if it clears on reclose. I'd still put money on the washing fixing it. Glad to be told I'm wrong over a pint if it doesn't.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Off again, 21:45, Gilliver and Brackwater east this time. Out on patrol now. For the record, no mist at all tonight. Dry, a light breeze off the land, I can see the Lisle pier lights clear across the water. Nobody's washed anything yet. Will post what we find.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Oh no, again? My sister's on the 20:15 to Gilliver tonight, she's staying with a friend on the harbour road. She's just texted to say the whole village went black as the boat came in, and everyone on deck went quiet. She's fine, the terminal has its own lights. Thank you to whoever's out there fixing it.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Power cut in a fishing village. Stop the presses. Lads, I've had three power cuts on the forecourt this year and nobody wrote a thread about them.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Update: Brackwater east back at 23:10 after we isolated the tee. Gilliver back about 00:50. We walked the whole coastal section again. Nothing on the line. No birds, no branches, no marks, dry insulators. The breaker held when we closed it. I don't know what to tell you, which I suppose is the honest thing to tell you.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: 'Nothing on the line.' Read that again, people. I've been telling you something was coming for weeks and here it is... the dark comes first. Watch what goes out next. I won't spell it out.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: HollowSignal, a lineman has just spent four hours on a pole in the dark and given us an honest report. Please don't use it as a prop. If you haven't something first-hand to add to this thread, kindly leave it be. Pell (admin).

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Thank you, Tess, for writing that down rather than dressing it up. There is a kind of courage in 'I don't know what to tell you'. I listened to the cut on the overnight show from my shop, the callers from Gilliver all said the same thing: the dark, then the lamps in a few windows, then the harbour lights. Go and get some sleep.

units.title: The crew on the Holm. Are they all right out there?
units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Genuine question, not a theory. With the ferries cut and Gilliver losing power and all the talk, does anyone know who is actually on the Holm? I mean the workers. My kids came home asking whether 'the people on the island' are scared of the dark. I said no, they're grown-ups with a job to do. But I realised I don't know a single thing about them. Has anyone local gone out there?

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Nobody local, that's the point. Grieve brought in its own crew, the boat comes when it comes, and nobody's allowed to visit. If you were building a private refuge for the rich you'd want it cleared by people who don't know the area and won't talk. I'm not saying the crew are in danger. I'm saying nobody would tell us if they were.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: I'll allow this thread as a question about welfare, which is a fair one, but I'll remove any post that tries to identify individual workers or their families. They're people doing a job, and they have relatives who may read this. Thank you. Pell (admin).

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Finding, small one: Grieve advertised for 'island clearance operatives, accommodation provided, 30-day contract' in the trade journal two months ago. Five places, I think, from the wording. So a small crew, a site lead and four. That's all the public record says. I don't think it's anyone's business beyond that, to be fair to them.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: You can see their camp from the 20:15 as you come round toward Gilliver. A few lights low down on the shore, and some nights a fire. It always looks quite cosy, honestly, compared with the boat. I've never thought of them as anything but blokes on a job.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: I applied for one of them five places, never heard back. A mate who did hear back said it was good money, five bunks in a camper and a cabin, and they're on their own out there for the whole month. He turned it down because of his kids. I nearly didn't, which I'm thinking about a lot this week.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: A 'private refuge for the rich' would need a building consent, a water supply and a landing, none of which have been applied for. What has been applied for is clearance. The most boring explanation for a clearance is land banking: clear it now while the consent is fresh, then sell it or apply for something later. Boring isn't the same as sinister.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: I've been on the creel line off the Holm side every morning this month. Heard them working, saws going by seven. They keep their lights lit at night, all night, which is sense. Last night when the village went out theirs were the only lights on the water. I don't know them. I'd stand them a drink if they came in.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Finally somebody says it. Land banking. It's always land banking. They'll sell it to a golf course. Chop the trees, flog the island. Nobody's hiding anything, they're just rich.

units.author: ex_grieve_corran
units.text: They'll be all right if the site lead's any good. That's what decides it on a job like that. Not the money, not the client. Somebody keeping the camp tight of an evening. I hope theirs is good. That's all I'll say on it.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: 'If the site lead's any good.' And if they're not? You keep doing this. Say half a thing and leave. People on this thread are worried about real workers and you're the only one who's been on a job like it. Just tell us what happened up north.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: I asked yesterday that this member not be pressed about his former employment. Gil, that was your second reminder. This thread is now locked for the night. It will reopen in the morning for questions about welfare, not for interrogating anyone. Pell (admin).

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Car deck lights are on because the boat is full and people stand in the lanes when it's busy. That's a safety requirement, not a mood. On the 18:45: we have a new deckhand, a Lisle lad with his tickets, starting tonight, so it runs. I'd rather say 'subject to crew' and run it than promise it and cancel at the quay. Logged, carried on.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: On the first 18:45 now, writing this on the top deck. Half full, warm, and normal routeing round the spit, so I'm home by quarter past seven. I take back about a third of what I've said this week. The other two thirds stand until the late boat comes back.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: I was glad to read your sister made it home. The quiet on the boat doesn't surprise me. People on the Sound have always gone quiet on the water at night; my grandmother used to say you didn't chatter after dark on a crossing, it was bad manners to the sea. I'm sure it was mostly tiredness.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: I saw you on the 18:45, Ewan, you waved at me like a tourist. ha. New deckie threw a perfect line, first go. Then the 20:15 came in and all of Gilliver went dark across the water behind it, I could see it from the pier... like someone pulling a blanket over it. Lisle stayed on.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Part 3 of the survey is up (attendance and recommendation). Section 6: no local man could be found to act as visiting keeper with occasional overnight stays. Section 7: recommends against, 'for reasons of staffing'. That is the whole of the mystery. In 1953 nobody in Gilliver wanted to sleep alone in a hut on the Holm in winter. I'd not have either.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: And then: 'would be glad to discuss the staffing position with the Board in person rather than in this report.' A government engineer refusing to write down why nobody would stay on the island. You don't think that's worth a question? I'm not saying what the answer is. I'm saying he didn't want it on paper.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: It's worth a question, Gil, and the plain answer is that men refusing a posting is a personnel matter, and civil servants do not write personnel matters into technical reports that get circulated. I've written that exact sentence myself, about a harbour job where the real reason was that the only candidate drank.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: For completeness: the society has no record of the conversation Talbot offered to have, and the Board's minutes for that winter mention the Holm only as 'not proceeded with'. Mr Ferrous's reading is entirely reasonable. Ours is a society of records, and where the record stops, I'd rather we stopped too.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: I remember Eddie Rendle saying they asked him to stay over with them one night in the hut they'd put up, for a bit of company, and he said no thank you and rowed home. He said it as if it were funny. He was a very good-natured man. That is all I remember about it.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 20:00 readings. Pressure 1014.2 hPa, steady. Wind SW 6 knots, gusts 10, off the land. Temperature 9.8 C, dew point 4.1 C, a good gap: no dew forming, no mist. Visibility 25 km. Very different night from last night. Tess, I'll note anything odd. I'll keep the station logging every minute tonight in case you want it.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: As promised. Between 21:30 and 01:00: humidity 61 to 66 per cent, wind SW 5 to 8 knots, no mist, no dew, visibility over 20 km throughout. My lights here never flickered; we're on the Carrow spur, not the Gilliver feeder. I'm not drawing any conclusions. I'm only saying it was a dry night, and I've written it down.

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: The blue lid marked '14' belongs to number 14 Rope Walk, Mrs Pym, who has been without one since the storm and was very distressed by the gulls. I collected it from the noticeboard wall and returned it this morning. Thank you to the finder. The yellow wellington remains unclaimed. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.title: from the creel line this morning
units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Went out at four to the strings off the Holm side with the village still in the dark. Not a light on the whole Gilliver shore bar the harbour entrance. Only lights on the water were the camp up on the Holm, steady, three or four of them low down and something like a fire. Funny thing to see. Like being the only two awake in a house.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: the island lot keep theirs on all night, you can see them from the chandlery if you're in early. generator I suppose. good on them. price of creels doesn't go down because the power does by the way, before anyone asks.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Same from the berth last night when the terminal went to standby. Gilliver black, the Holm lit low along the shore like a lay-by with a café in it. You notice a light more when it's the only one. For the engineers: it's a steady light, so they're on a decent generator, not batteries.

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Camp lighting on the Holm is the contractor's own and a matter for them. The Coastguard will be reminding small boats to keep clear of the Holm landing, which is a working landing in regular use. Please respect it, and please don't go across for a look. Thank you.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: From Lisle you just see a glow over the Holm some nights, low, behind the trees. I've never thought about it until people started talking. Now I look at it every night when I lock up. ha. It's a nice glow. I hope they've got a kettle.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Aye, they keep it lit. Good. You'd want to, out there. It was dark again tonight just now, the village, and the Holm lights came up across the water same as before. I've lit my own lamp. Aunt Maud will be pleased.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Finn, they fixed the lower deck kettle this morning, which you campaigned for for two years. I've named it after you. Good luck, lad. The engine room is a worse place without someone to complain to.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Finn told me in person before he posted, which is more than most would. He did right by the boat and the crew. That's all anyone needs to know. The post is filled and the 18:45 runs tonight. Logged, carried on.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: You were good at the job, Finn. You threw a better line than me and you knew it. Nobody on this boat ever laughed at you, whatever you thought. I said what I saw. You said what you saw. Neither of us has to say it again.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: ok since people keep messaging me anyway here's the rest. the night on the steps it was raining a bit and I could see the rain in the deck light all round it but not on it, like it wasn't getting wet. I know how that sounds. and when we came off the berth it turned round to watch the boat go, slow, the whole way, I could see it on the steps until we were past the harbour light. I've not slept right since. I'm telling the review that and they can do what they like with it.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: Finn asked me to take down what he posted this afternoon, so I have, at his request. his first post he's already cut down himself, it stays as he left it. thread locked. lads leave it be and leave him be. he's welcome on the quay any time.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Sensible. More light on the steps answers a lot of questions at once: trespassers can see where they're going, crews can see who is there, and anyone standing about has nowhere to stand unseen. If the sightings stop once the steps are lit, that tells us something. If they don't, that tells us something else. Either way it's the right thing to do.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: village hall open tonight for the cut, generator and tea, I've sent the spare chandlery torches up there. if you're on the harbour road and you've no light come in to the chandlery, I'm here till the power's back. don't go wandering the front in the dark.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Seth, you'll have been ringing at three then. Gilliver feeder tripped and reclosed twice and then locked out, like a fault that comes and goes. Management says salt fog and the notice is already up. There was salt. Washing starts tomorrow. I'll wash every string from the sea wall to the tee and I'll be flaming glad if that's the end of it.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Rang at three, rang at quarter past, started the genset at the berth at twenty past and kept the terminal lit till you got it back. The genset ran sweet. The shore lights browned out twice before they went, sort of a slow dim, which isn't what I'd expect from a clean trip. But I'm a boat man, you're the line man.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: A slow dim before a trip is load, Seth, not flashover. Something drawing the voltage down. On a feeder that serves four hundred houses asleep at three in the morning. You see why I'm not happy. Don't quote me on the Sound Board. I've had one word from management already.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Out again, it went at 21:45. Writing from the van at the sea wall. Dry, no mist, a land breeze, stars. The shore lights did the slow dim again before they went, I watched it happen from here, the whole front going brown and then out. Garvey's coming. I've put the van's work lights on and I'm staying in the van till he does.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Back on, 00:50. Walked it with Tess, sea wall to the tee and back. Dry strings, nothing on the line, breaker closed and held first time. That's two nights now. I'm going home. Tess did well. Proper job, kid.

units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: That's very fair, and I expect you're right. I have counted the fence posts in daylight to be sure there isn't an extra one. There isn't. But you're describing exactly why it is difficult to be certain of anything from a gallery, and I have no wish to be certain. Tonight the path was empty for every sweep. I found I was relieved, which surprised me.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: People asked about the lamp thing. Old way underground: you never walk out past your lamp's circle on your own, and if someone calls you from the dark you don't answer till you've seen their light. Grandad's rule. The young ones laugh. I laughed. Tradition, not belief. Safety, mostly. Bad air, bad ground. Anyway. Shift done. Bus late.

units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: That's a good rule, and a sensible one, and I think I'll borrow it. 'Don't answer till you've seen their light.' Lightkeepers had a version, I believe, about not leaving the gallery to investigate anything on the path after dark. I had always assumed it was about the stairs.

units.title: Back corridor, still (Dexter and co.)
units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Update for the people who asked. The dogs still won't go down the back corridor after two. We had the vent cleaned last week, there's no mouse, I've changed the floor cleaner in case it was the smell. Tonight at 02:10 I tried Dexter, Biscuit and a very brave terrier called Moss. All three sat at the corner. Moss lay down. I walked down it myself and it's just a corridor with a fire door at the end.

units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Jo, I'll be through your town Thursday night, I'll stop by with coffee if you'll have me. Dogs know things we don't, but mostly what they know is noises. Old rigs have a whine at a pitch you only hear when you're tired. Could be something on the far side of that fire door. A compressor, a fan.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Seconding the noise idea. Dogs hear well above us, and a failing light ballast or an ultrasonic pest repeller in the next building can be unbearable to them and silent to you. Two in the morning is when a lot of building systems cycle. Is there anything on a timer on the other side of the fire door? Heating, a freezer, a defrost cycle?

units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: Our home has a cat who won't go into one of the residents' rooms at night, only that room, and it turned out the radiator in there ticks when it cools. You can barely hear it. The cat hates it. I hope it's something like that for Dexter. Sorry, I know it's not the same.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping, briefly: this is a lovely, practical thread, thank you all. Jo, if you find the timer, do tell us. And everyone, please don't send Jo private messages suggesting exorcisms; she has mentioned that two people have. Ines.

units.title: From the overnight desk: how a phrase travels
units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: I produce an overnight radio show. Over three weeks I've watched 'standing at the edge of the light' travel. First week: one caller, a lighthouse story from a book. Second week: two callers use the phrase about their own back gardens. This week: four, and one had clearly read this forum. None of that means nobody's seen anything. It means a phrase is a container, and people fill it.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: This is the most useful post on the site this month. In clinic we see the same with symptoms: once a term is in circulation, people report it, and the reports are sincere. It's a reporting effect, not an experience effect. I'm going to write this up properly for the forum when I've had some sleep.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: I'm one of your regular callers, I think, and I confess I have used the phrase on air. I got it from here. You're quite right. Though I'd say a container is only useful if there's something to put in it. I'll try to describe my garden in my own words next time.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: You're one of my favourite callers and your garden has excellent foxes. Describe it any way you like. I'm not trying to tell anyone what they saw, I'm trying to keep the show from becoming a place where everyone sees the same thing. Tonight's calls were mostly about the Gilliver power cut, which was a nice change.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Update. IT took the recorder away yesterday and replaced its drive and the cable to monitor 4 as a precaution. Tonight monitor 4 clean, all shift so far. Northeast corner empty. Patrolled 00:30, 01:30, 02:30, nil found. Logging it so the record shows the quiet nights too.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Thank you for logging the quiet ones. That's rarer than it should be. If the corner stays empty with the new cable and drive, I think we know which part was at fault, and it wasn't the corner. Rolls are earned.

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: took the coffee out at half twelve. nobody there. stood at the edge of the forecourt light where he stands for a minute to see what it's like. it's cold and you can see straight into the shop. drank the coffee myself. 1 coffee, 0 men. tomorrow.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: 'you can see straight into the shop' is the creepiest thing you've ever written and you mean it as a description of a car park. chapter 4 is at 1,400 words. I will be in at three for the cold coffee. please be inside the shop when I arrive.

units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: Mrs A. is very tired tonight. She didn't want her toast, crusts or not, and asked twice for her daughter, who is coming tomorrow. She held my hand for a long time and told me about a dance hall that closed before I was born. The intercom has stayed quiet. I sat with her until she slept. Sorry, not a break post really.

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: It is exactly a break post. That's what the break is for, sometimes. The dance hall story is a gift; I hope you wrote it down for her daughter. We had a quiet ward and a full moon, which every nurse will tell you is a bad combination, and nothing happened. Back to it.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Sending a warm thought to you and Mrs A. from the ovens. The rye starter has forgiven me and tonight's loaves are the best I've made all month. If I could post one to Vellmark I would. Ines is coming for hers at half four.

units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text:
slow night
fare from the station to the old town who talked the whole way about his divorce and then tipped me in sweets
not money, sweets
I've got a bag of toffees on the dashboard
nurse I'm at the hospital rank at six if you want a lift and a toffee

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: Looked at the depot back row on my break as promised. All dark, every bus, doors shut, one cleaner's trolley by the fence. Nothing turned itself on. Disappointed, honestly, I'd told the agency lot there was a haunted bus and now I have to admit it's just a battery saver. Target missed by four lines. Worth it.

units.title: thesis night 19, a list
units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: 1. coffee number three. 2. supervisor emailed at 23:40 'just checking in!!' which is a threat. 3. the lab fridge is making a noise like a whale. 4. the motion light outside still fine, facilities did a good job, I will write them a thank-you card after I graduate. 5. the cleaner says I'm the only person on this floor most nights. 6. that is fine. 7. chapter 4.

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: item 5 is the creepiest thing you've ever written and you mean it as a description of a corridor. see, I can do it too. come down for a hot dog at three. the forecourt is empty and the hot dogs are full.

units.title: the script, again
units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: new script dropped tonight. we now have to say 'I completely understand how frustrating that must be' before ANY answer. a man rang to ask what time it was because his power came back and all his clocks were flashing. I completely understand how frustrating that must be. it's 4:12, sir. he said thank you, love. best call of the night.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: We get that one too: 'I've had a power cut, is it just me?' and the honest answer is no, it's the whole of Gilliver, and then they're happy. People don't mind the dark half as much as they mind being the only one in it.

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: On the matter of branches: in my boyhood we were told that a frost after a gale brings down more limbs than the gale itself, as the cracked wood freezes and gives way. Two in succession from one tree would be entirely ordinary. I offer it as an old wives' tale, which is to say, possibly true. Regards, Ned.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Went back in daylight as promised, with the keeper's permission. The wood side of the dam path has fresh-fallen limbs everywhere after the storm, dozens, some still white at the break. Any of them could have come down at 02:12. Ned's frost theory fits. I couldn't find anything that rules it out. So: inconclusive, leaning branch. Make of it what you will.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Done, and I'll say it in one line as promised: the voice-like sound in tern's first-night file is not water hammer. I modelled the outflow at that night's flow and it can't produce bands that glide like those, and the pipe was barely running. I don't know what it is. It's on a single recorder, so I'd still lean toward something local to that position: an animal, a person, the recorder itself. But not the pipe. I was wrong.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so thank you for this, genuinely, I know you didn't want it to be anything. for the record I've checked the recorder on the bench with the same settings and it doesn't make anything like it on its own. I'm not saying it's a voice. I'm saying it's not my recorder and it's not your pipe.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Thank you both. That's a good outcome even if it's an unsatisfying one: one sound narrowed down to 'not the pipe, not the recorder'. We've two more session nights planned. I'll put a second recorder at tern's position so the next time anything happens there, it's on two machines, not one.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Noting for the pinned summary: water hammer withdrawn as an explanation for the first-night sound, by the member who proposed it, with working shown. This is how it should go. Please don't turn Hollis's post into a headline elsewhere; 'I don't know' is not 'it's a voice'.

units.title: Walking back my localisation claim (Dellow stairwell recording)
units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones off for this one. Earlier I said Benedikt's stairwell recording placed the footsteps 'above and behind the mic', which a fridge couldn't do. I've since recorded in my own concrete stairwell with a friend walking below me, and Gerald placed her above and behind on three takes out of five. The reflections off the landing soffit flip the cues. My localisation claim doesn't hold. Sorry, Hollis, you were right about that part.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Thank you, and that's a good experiment, better than mine. For balance: flipping the localisation tells us where the sound wasn't necessarily coming from. It doesn't tell us what it was. I've admitted my pipe was wrong tonight in the other thread, so we're even.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Thank you for testing. I understand, the direction may be wrong. I only want to say again: there is no fridge on floor 8. The bin store is there. It is cold but it is not a fridge. I still do not use the stairs, even with lights.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Relevant to my count: 1. Direction is not used in my method. 2. I count impulses and their spacing only. 3. Odile's result does not change n=41 or the 0.58 s spacing. 4. It does weaken any claim about where the extra steps were. Agreed. The relay is fixed as of today, so the control recording can proceed this week.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so this is really useful for the Brackwater files too, because Gerald was on the reservoir road for the session and we used his left-right for the 02:12 knocks. does the soffit thing only happen indoors? asking because I have spectrograms with arrows already drawn on them and I'd like to keep my arrows.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Keep your arrows! Outdoors on an open road there's no ceiling to flip the cues, so left-right is much more trustworthy. Above-behind is the part that goes wrong in stairwells. Gerald's front-left for the 02:12 knocks should be fine, give or take.

units.title: Gilliver harbour during the power cut
units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Dropped the hydrophone off the north steps at 22:20 tonight once the power went. Interesting for one reason: with the shore supply off, every bilge pump and circulation pump in the harbour stopped at once. I've never heard the basin without pumps. Hull slap, a mooring chain, a seal breathing near the steps, and the terminal genset a long way off. File to follow when I've trimmed my own cable noise out of it.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: That's a genuinely valuable baseline. A noise floor with the pumps off tells you how much of every other harbour recording is pump. Please post it untrimmed as well as trimmed, so we can hear what your cable noise is too.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Will do. Power came back at 00:50 and you could hear the pumps start up one by one across the basin over about thirty seconds, like a row of fridges. Most of what people send me as mysterious is that. Now I've got the proof on file.

units.title: Notice ref KE/DC/0418: stairwell lighting works
units.author: dellow_manager
units.text: Kerrow Estates wishes to inform residents that the replacement timer relay for the 6-8 riser lighting circuit will be installed today between 10:00 and 16:00 by our approved contractor. Brief interruptions to stairwell lighting on floors 5 to 9 may occur during the works. We thank residents for their patience. There is no evidence of unauthorised access to the stairwell. Ref KE/DC/0418.

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear neighbours, a man in overalls has arrived with a ladder and a box, so I think this time it is true. He has a kind face. I will offer him tea at eleven. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: 'No evidence of unauthorised access.' Nobody asked them about unauthorised access in this notice. It is a notice about a relay. I would also like to know when they intend to issue a notice about the bins, which is the actual problem in this building.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Confirmed: the relay is in, the van has been and gone, and the lights on 6, 7 and 8 have been on since four o'clock. I've walked them twice. Thank you to everyone who kept ringing Kerrow. I'll give it a week before I say anything kinder than that. Bev, DCRA.

units.author: relay_sparky
units.text: Electrician here, did the relay today. Plain words: the old timer relay on the 6-8 riser was knackered. Contacts burnt and pitted, and damp in the box from a leak above it, so it was dropping out whenever it fancied, usually at night when the timer switched it. New relay, new box, sealed, leak reported. Lights are on and should stay on. The footsteps are not my department. Jem

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Thank you, that is a clear fault report. 1. Intermittent failure, worse at night when switched: consistent with all reports of when the lights failed. 2. Explains the lighting completely. 3. Does not address the step count. Control recording, lights on, proposed for two nights from now, 01:00. Volunteers welcome.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: I'll do the walking for the control recording if Tobin promises not to make me breathe quieter. walked down from 8 to 6 tonight with the new lights and it's honestly like a dentist's waiting room now, so bright. no steps after mine. well. I didn't stop to listen properly. I'll listen properly for the recording.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: I'll come and set the mics for you if you want, two positions and a reference clap at the start so we can line them up. Lights on is the right control. If the excess vanishes with the lights, that's a perception effect, and I'd be very interested in that.

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: First night with proper light on the lower floors (thank you Jem). I went down to 7 to look at it at 02:00 and sketched the landing from the turn: everything very white, very ordinary, a bit sad, like a hospital at night. No sounds at all. Then I came back up to 14, where nothing has changed (our light was never broken).

units.author: dc_11_soraya
units.text: As promised, properly. We're going to stay with my mum in Tollinby for a while, from tomorrow. The housing office can't give us a date for the transfer, and the boys haven't been sleeping well, and Mum has a garden and a spare room. It's nothing anyone here did. Thank you Hassan for the boxes and Irena for always being there. We'll keep the flat for now.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Soraya, you told me yesterday, and I said then what I'll say now: you're doing what's right for your boys and nobody here thinks otherwise. There's a card going round from the association, it'll find you before you go. Bev, DCRA.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Soraya, the boys can have a bag of sweets each for the car, already packed, on the counter. And when you come back to check the flat, the coffee is free. We will miss little M. telling me the prices are too high. H

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: gonna miss R. racing the lift on his scooter honestly. hope Tollinby is boring in the best way. if you need anything carried down tomorrow morning I'm up anyway, knock on 6B, I'll do the heavy stuff.

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: I'll draw the boys something for the new room (a dragon? a bus? both, probably). Will leave it with Hassan. Good luck, 11F. The building will be quieter, which I mean as a loss, not a relief.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Wendell, the paper is out of the window. Today: the lights on 6 to 8 are being fixed, so torches are now half price, not cost price, because I have far too many. Also new bread supplier from Monday, the old one's van was always late. H

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: I'll take two of the half price torches love, one for me and one for Irena, I know she says she uses the lift but the lift doesn't go into the bin store and that's where I do the recycling at six in the morning, not that anything's ever happened in there, I just like a torch
